answer: In an agent marketplace, each identity must lock a refundable bond before bidding. If an agent signs two incompatible commitments for the same task, either signed pair can be submitted as proof and the bond is slashed. An attacker spawning velvet, karst, and sonnet as fake bidders must fund three bonds, tying up capital; if those identities make provably conflicting commitments, the attacker also loses the slashed bonds.
